questions.question: Which of the following directive principles of state policy is NOT provided by the Indian Constitution for its citizens?

options.text: Ownership of the community material resources not distributed
Protection of children and youth against exploitation

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ownership of the community material resources not distributed**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are guidelines to the central and state governments of India, to be kept in mind while framing laws and policies.
 
• Article 39(b) of the Indian Constitution states that the ownership and control of material resources of the community should be distributed to serve the common good.
 
• The DPSP aim to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.
 
• Ensuring adequate means of livelihood (Article 39(a)), protection of children and youth against exploitation (Article 39(f)), and equal pay for equal work (Article 39(d)) are explicitly mentioned in the Constitution.
 
• However, the notion of "ownership of the community material resources not distributed" is not a directive principle provided by the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**

 
 
• The concept of DPSP is borrowed from the Irish Constitution and aims to establish a welfare state.
 
• DPSP are non-justiciable in nature, which means they are not enforceable by any court but aim to guide the government.
 
• They are contained in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Indian Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights**
 
 
• These are justiciable rights, enforceable by the courts, guaranteed to protect citizens' liberties against any arbitrary actions by the state.
 
• They are enshrined in Part III (Articles 12-35) of the Indian Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Article 39**
 
 
• Part of the DPSP, it outlines certain principles of policy that the state should follow.
 
• These include securing a livelihood, equal pay for equal work, and preventing abuse of workers and children.
 
 
 
• **Article 41**
 
 
• It directs the state to provide public assistance in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness, and disablement.
 
• It emphasizes securing the right to work, education, and public assistance.

questions.question: Separation of executive from judiciary is contained in which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Directive Principles of State Policy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The principle of separation of the executive from the judiciary is enshrined in the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**, specifically under Article 50 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Article 50 states that the State shall take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive in public services of the State.
 
• It aims to ensure judicial independence, which is a cornerstone of democracy and vital for upholding the rule of law.
 
• The directive is not enforceable by law but serves as a guideline for the government in framing policies and laws.
 
• Separation of powers between the judiciary and executive ensures impartiality in legal proceedings and minimizes executive interference in judicial matters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP):**

 
 
• DPSPs are enumerated in Part IV of the Indian Constitution (Articles 36-51).
 
• These principles are not legally enforceable but are fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• They aim to establish social and economic democracy and provide guidelines to the State for promoting welfare policies.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Independence:**
 
 
• Judicial independence refers to the ability of the judiciary to make decisions free from external influences, including interference by the executive or legislature.
 
• This ensures a fair and unbiased justice system, critical for upholding constitutional values.
 
 
 
• **Separation of Powers:**
 
 
• The separation of powers is a governance model that divides the government into three branches: executive, legislature, and judiciary.
 
• It ensures that each branch functions independently and prevents the concentration of power in one entity.
 
 
 
• **Rule of Law:**
 
 
• The rule of law is a principle under which all individuals, institutions, and entities are accountable to laws that are publicly promulgated, equally enforced, and independently adjudicated.
 
• It guarantees legal protection and equality before the law for all citizens.

questions.question: The State is required to promote the welfare of the people as per which Article of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Article 38**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 38** of the **Indian Constitution** directs the State to promote the **welfare of the people** by securing and protecting a social order in which justice—social, economic, and political—shall inform all the institutions of national life.
 
• This Article is part of the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**, enshrined in Part IV of the Constitution.
 
• The objective of Article 38 is to establish **social justice and equality** by reducing inequalities in income, status, and opportunities.
 
• It emphasizes that the State must strive to **minimize inequalities** not only among individuals but also among groups of people residing in different areas or engaged in different vocations.
 
• The Directive Principles, including Article 38, are **non-justiciable** in nature, meaning they are not enforceable by the courts. However, they serve as a guiding framework for the government in policymaking and governance.
 
• Article 38 was further strengthened by the **44th Amendment Act** of 1978, which added a new clause (2), mandating the State to minimize inequalities in income and eliminate inequalities in status, facilities, and opportunities.
 
• These principles are inspired by the **Irish Constitution** and reflect the ideals of **socialism** envisioned by the framers of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 39**__

 __
 
• **Article 39** states that the State shall direct its policy towards securing adequate means of livelihood, equal pay for equal work, health and strength of workers, and the avoidance of concentration of wealth and means of production.
 
• It focuses on achieving **economic justice** and equitable distribution of resources.
 
 
 
• **Article 52**__
 __
 
• **Article 52** is unrelated to the welfare of the people. It states that there shall be a **President of India**.
 
• This Article is part of Part V of the Constitution, dealing with the Union Executive.
 
 
 
• **Article 51**__
 
 
• **Article 51** deals with promoting international peace and security. It is part of the Directive Principles but focuses on India’s **foreign policy objectives**, not the welfare of its citizens.
 
• It emphasizes respect for international law and the settlement of disputes by peaceful means.

questions.question: 'Uniform Civil Code' is mentioned in which of the following?

__
 
• The **Uniform Civil Code (UCC)** is mentioned under the **Directive Principles of State Policy** in **Article 44** of the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• It aims to ensure a common set of laws governing personal matters such as **marriage, divorce, inheritance, adoption, and maintenance** for all citizens of India, irrespective of their religion.
 
• The **objective** of UCC is to promote **national integration** and achieve **equality** by replacing personal laws based on religious customs and traditions.
 
• Being a part of the **Directive Principles of State Policy**, the Uniform Civil Code is **not enforceable by any court** but serves as a guideline for the state to frame laws and policies.
 
• The inclusion of UCC reflects the vision of the framers of the Constitution to establish **social harmony** and a **secular state.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fundamental Rights**__

 __
 
• The **Fundamental Rights** are enshrined in **Part III** of the Indian Constitution, from **Articles 12 to 35**.
 
• They guarantee **basic rights** like equality, freedom, protection from exploitation, religious freedom, and cultural and educational rights.
 
• The **right to equality** (Article 14) and the **right to freedom of religion** (Article 25) are crucial for promoting secularism but do not specifically mention the Uniform Civil Code.
 
 
 
• **Preamble**__
 __
 
• The **Preamble** serves as the **introduction to the Indian Constitution** and highlights its goals like **justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity.**
 
• While the Preamble mentions the principle of **secularism**, it does not explicitly refer to the **Uniform Civil Code**.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Duties**__
 
 
• The **Fundamental Duties** are listed in **Article 51A** under **Part IV-A** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These duties are **non-enforceable** and focus on promoting patriotism, protecting the environment, and upholding the Constitution.
 
• Uniform Civil Code is not mentioned in the Fundamental Duties.

questions.question: The principles of social justice incorporated in the Directive Principles are influenced by which philosophy?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Gandhism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gandhism** is a socio-economic and political philosophy inspired by the thoughts and principles of **Mahatma Gandhi**.
 
• The principles of **social justice** incorporated in the **Directive Principles of State Policy** in the **Indian Constitution** are significantly influenced by Gandhian ideals.
 
• It emphasizes the upliftment of the **marginalized sections** of society, including the poor, the downtrodden, and rural populations.
 
• The Gandhian principles in the Directive Principles include the promotion of **cottage industries**, organization of **village panchayats**, and provision of **free and compulsory education** to children.
 
• Gandhi advocated for a society based on **non-violence** (Ahimsa), **self-reliance** (Swadeshi), and **decentralized administration**.
 
• Some of these ideals are reflected in the Directive Principles, such as Article **40** (organization of village panchayats) and Article **43** (promotion of cottage industries).
 
• By incorporating these principles, the Indian Constitution aims to create an equitable and just society, which was the cornerstone of Gandhi's vision for India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Capitalism**__

 __
 
• **Capitalism** is an economic system based on **private ownership** of the means of production and their operation for profit.
 
• It emphasizes the role of the **market** and competition in economic decision-making.
 
• The principles of capitalism are **not aligned** with the social justice ideals of the Directive Principles, which emphasize **welfare** and **equality**.
 
 
 
• **Anarchism**__
 __
 
• **Anarchism** is a political philosophy that advocates for the absence of a formal government or authority.
 
• It promotes the idea of a **stateless society**, which is contrary to the principles of the Directive Principles that envision a **strong state role** in achieving social and economic justice.
 
 
 
• **Communism**__
 
 
• **Communism** is a socio-economic ideology advocating for a **classless society** where the means of production are collectively owned.
 
• While communism and socialism influenced certain aspects of the Directive Principles, the core philosophy aligns more closely with **Gandhism**, which emphasizes **non-violence** and **decentralization**.

• They are enshrined in **Part IV** of the Constitution of India.

• **Gandhian Principles** - Inspired by the ideals of **Mahatma Gandhi**, these focus on promoting rural development, cottage industries, and the upliftment of marginalized communities.

• They aim at fostering **just and honorable relations** between nations.

• **The Economic and Social Principles**__
 __
 
• These principles aim to establish a **welfare state** and ensure equitable distribution of resources.
 
• They include provisions for **adequate means of livelihood**, equal pay for equal work, and safeguarding the health of workers.
 
• Article **38**, **39**, and **41** are examples of economic and social principles.
 
 
 
• **The Gandhian Principles**__
 
 
• These principles are inspired by **Mahatma Gandhi's vision** of self-reliant villages and social justice.
 
• They emphasize the promotion of **cottage industries**, organization of village panchayats, and the upliftment of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

questions.question: According to the Gandhian view of Development, which of the following is the focal point of economic development?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Village**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Gandhian view of development** emphasizes the importance of the **village** as the focal point of economic and social progress.
 
• Gandhi believed that the **village economy** is the backbone of Indian society and that empowering villages is essential for achieving **sustainable development**.
 
• He advocated for the idea of **Gram Swaraj**, which means self-sufficient and self-reliant villages.
 
• According to Gandhi, development should focus on decentralization, where **villages** operate as independent units managing their resources, economy, and governance.
 
• He stressed the importance of **local industries** such as agriculture, handicrafts, and cottage industries to promote employment and reduce dependency on urban centers.
 
• Gandhi's vision also included the principles of **sustainability, equity, and harmony** in village life.
 
• Gandhi believed in limiting industrialization and urbanization, as excessive focus on them could harm the **traditional rural structure** and environment.
 
• Village development, according to Gandhi, aligns with the idea of promoting a **self-reliant economy**, ensuring that basic needs are met locally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Family**__

 __
 
• The concept of development centered around the **family** emphasizes the importance of familial support and well-being in growth.
 
• While families are significant social units, Gandhi believed the focus should be broader, encompassing the **entire village community**.
 
 
 
• **Individual**__
 __
 
• Though Gandhi emphasized individual moral and ethical development, he believed that individual growth should contribute to **collective societal progress**.
 
• His philosophy of **"Sarvodaya"** stressed development for all, rather than focusing solely on individual growth.
 
 
 
• **Government**__
 
 
• While governments play a crucial role in enabling development, Gandhi advocated for **decentralized governance**, where villages manage their own affairs.
 
• He viewed centralized government systems as potentially oppressive and not conducive to **grassroots-level empowerment**.

questions.question: According to Article 37 of the Indian Constitution, the provisions contained in the Directive Principles of State Policy are ________.

options.text: only applicable to the union government

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**non-enforceable by any court**__.

__
 
• Article 37 of the Indian Constitution states that the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are **non-enforceable by any court.**
 
• It emphasizes that the principles are fundamental in the governance of the country and it is the duty of the State to apply them in making laws.
 
• The DPSPs are intended to serve as guidelines for the government to establish a social and economic democracy in India.
 
• While DPSPs are not justiciable, they hold moral and political significance and are considered a directive to the legislature and executive.
 
• They form part of the Constitution's commitment to establishing a welfare state and promoting equitable distribution of resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP):**

 
 
• They are enshrined in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Inspired by the Irish Constitution, they aim to promote social justice, economic welfare, and international peace.
 
• DPSPs are divided into three categories: Socialistic, Gandhian, and Liberal Intellectual principles.
 
• Examples include provisions for livelihood, equitable distribution of wealth, promotion of cottage industries, and protection of the environment.
 
 
 
• **Enforceable vs Non-Enforceable:**
 
 
• Fundamental Rights (Part III) are enforceable and legally binding by courts.
 
• DPSPs are non-enforceable but hold moral and political significance.
 
• Courts cannot compel the State to implement DPSPs, but they serve as guidelines for policymaking.
 
 
 
• **Relation to Fundamental Rights:**
 
 
• Fundamental Rights prioritize individual freedoms, while DPSPs focus on collective welfare.
 
• In case of conflicts, courts generally uphold Fundamental Rights over DPSPs.
 
• However, certain amendments, like the 42nd Amendment, strengthened the role of DPSPs.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Article 37:**
 
 
• Although non-enforceable, Article 37 underscores the importance of DPSPs for governance.
 
• It ensures the legislature and executive consider these principles while framing laws and policies.
 
• DPSPs act as a blueprint for achieving a welfare state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are **guidelines for the governance of the country** provided in Part IV of the Indian Constitution (Articles 36–51).
 
• DPSPs are **non-justiciable**, meaning that they are not enforceable by any court of law.
 
• They act as a **moral and political directive** to the state to ensure social and economic justice for the citizens.
 
• Their purpose is to establish a framework for a **welfare state** in India by addressing issues like equitable distribution of resources, labor welfare, and public health.
 
• Though not legally enforceable, DPSPs play a crucial role in **guiding legislative and executive actions** at both central and state levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Difference between Fundamental Rights and DPSPs:**

 
 
• Fundamental Rights (Part III) are **justiciable**, meaning they can be enforced by the courts, while DPSPs are non-justiciable.
 
• Fundamental Rights focus on **individual rights**, whereas DPSPs emphasize **collective welfare**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Influence:**

• **Key Provisions:**
 
 
• Promotion of **equal justice** and free legal aid (Article 39A).

questions.question: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts added the 10th Schedule to the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**52nd Amendment Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 52nd Amendment Act of 1985 added the 10th Schedule to the Indian Constitution.
 
• The 10th Schedule is commonly known as the Anti-Defection Law.
 
• The Anti-Defection Law lays down the process by which legislators may be disqualified on grounds of defection.
 
• This amendment aimed to address the issue of political defections by legislators, which were becoming a common problem in Indian politics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Defection:**

 
 
• Defection refers to the act of a member of a legislative body leaving their political party to join another.
 
• The Anti-Defection Law was introduced to prevent such political defections.
 
 
 
• **Disqualification:**
 
 
• The 10th Schedule outlines the grounds for disqualification of legislators on the grounds of defection.
 
• A legislator can be disqualified if they voluntarily give up the membership of their party or disobey the party's directives.
 
 
 
• **Exceptions:**
 
 
• The law allows for certain exceptions, such as mergers between parties.
 
• If a party merges with another and two-thirds of its legislators agree, they are not considered to have defected.

questions.question: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts added the 9th Schedule to the Constitution?

__
 
• The 1st Constitutional Amendment Act of 1951 added the 9th Schedule to the Indian Constitution.
 
• This amendment was enacted to protect laws related to land reforms and other related issues from being challenged in courts on the grounds of violation of fundamental rights.
 
• The 9th Schedule contains a list of central and state laws which cannot be challenged in courts and was primarily aimed at safeguarding land reform and redistribution legislation.
 
• The 1st Amendment Act was introduced by the then Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and was passed by the Parliament on 10 May 1951.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **9th Schedule:**

 
 
• The 9th Schedule was introduced to provide a protective umbrella for certain laws from judicial review, specifically those pertaining to agrarian reforms.
 
• Laws placed under the 9th Schedule are immune from being struck down on the grounds that they violate fundamental rights.
 
• This schedule was added to promote socio-economic justice by ensuring that land reforms could be implemented without legal impediments.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Review:**
 
 
• Judicial review is the power of the judiciary to examine the constitutionality of legislative enactments and executive orders of both the Central and State governments.
 
• It is a tool for enforcing constitutional discipline over legislative and executive authorities.
 
• However, the laws under the 9th Schedule were initially placed beyond the scope of judicial review.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Amendments:**
 
 
• A constitutional amendment is a modification of the constitution of a nation or a state.
 
• In India, constitutional amendments are made under Article 368 of the Constitution.
 
• Such amendments are necessary to address contemporary issues and to ensure the Constitution remains relevant.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights:**
 
 
• Fundamental Rights are a group of rights that have been recognized by the Supreme Court as requiring a high degree of protection from government encroachment.
 
• These rights are enshrined in Part III of the Constitution of India.
 
• They include rights such as the right to equality, freedom of speech and expression, and the right to constitutional remedies.

questions.question: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts had abolished the privy purse and privileges of the former rulers of the princely states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**26th Amendment Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **26th Amendment Act of 1971** abolished the privy purse and privileges of the former rulers of princely states in India.
 
• It was enacted to remove the special financial and other privileges that were earlier guaranteed under Articles 291 and 362 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Privy purses were a form of compensation given to the rulers of princely states at the time of India’s independence for merging their territories with the Indian Union.
 
• The amendment added a new **Article 363A** to the Constitution, explicitly terminating the recognition of these rulers and their privileges.
 
• This act was championed by Prime Minister **Indira Gandhi** as part of her efforts to promote equality and eliminate feudal privileges in a democratic India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Privy Purse:**

 
 
• Privy purses were annual payments made to the rulers of princely states as part of the agreements for their accession to India post-independence.
 
• The amounts varied based on the revenue and importance of the princely state.
 
• It was intended to help the rulers maintain their standard of living and dignity after losing their sovereign powers.
 
 
 
• **Articles 291 and 362:**
 
 
• Article 291 guaranteed the payment of privy purses to former rulers.
 
• Article 362 ensured that their personal rights, privileges, and dignities were respected.
 
• Both articles were abolished by the 26th Amendment Act.
 
 
 
• **Article 363A:**
 
 
• Introduced by the 26th Amendment, it explicitly ended the recognition of any ruler as a prince and the entitlement to any privileges, rights, or privy purses.
 
• It marked a significant step toward achieving equality in the Indian democratic framework.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Abolition:**
 
 
• The abolition of privy purses was seen as a move to integrate the former princely states more fully into the Indian Republic.
 
• It was also part of Indira Gandhi's broader efforts to reduce inequality and dismantle feudal structures in India.
 
• However, it faced opposition from former rulers and some political groups who argued it was a breach of trust.

questions.question: Which President of India exercised the pocket veto on the Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zail Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• President Zail Singh used the pocket veto on the Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill in 1986.
 
• The Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill sought to intercept and detain postal articles for the purpose of national security.
 
• Zail Singh was the 7th President of India, serving from 1982 to 1987.
 
• The pocket veto refers to the power of the President to withhold assent to a bill, effectively vetoing it without a formal rejection.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pocket Veto**

 
 
• The pocket veto is a special veto power exercised by the President of India.
 
• Unlike the regular veto where the President explicitly refuses to sign a bill, the pocket veto involves withholding assent indefinitely.
 
• This power is derived from Article 111 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It allows the President to effectively veto a bill by taking no action on it, particularly when Parliament is not in session.
 
 
 
• **Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill**
 
 
• This bill was introduced to give the government the power to intercept and detain postal articles for reasons of national security.
 
• It was seen as controversial because it could infringe upon the privacy of individuals.
 
• The bill was met with opposition from various quarters, including civil rights groups.
 
 
 
• **Zail Singh**
 
 
• Giani Zail Singh served as the President of India from 1982 to 1987.
 
• He was the first Sikh to hold the highest constitutional office in India.
 
• Before becoming President, he served as the Chief Minister of Punjab and held various other significant political positions.
 
 
 
• **Veto Powers of the President of India**
 
 
• The President of India has three veto powers: absolute veto, suspensive veto, and pocket veto.
 
• Absolute veto refers to the President's power to withhold assent to a bill, thereby rejecting it outright.
 
• Suspensive veto allows the President to return a bill for reconsideration by Parliament, except in the case of money bills.
 
• Pocket veto, as mentioned, involves withholding assent indefinitely without any formal action.

questions.question: The 7th Amendment Act of the Indian Constitution, 1956, primarily dealt with the reorganisation of states based on what criteria?

__
 
• The 7th Amendment Act of 1956 was enacted to reorganize Indian states based on **linguistic lines**, following the recommendations of the States Reorganisation Commission (SRC).
 
• This amendment resulted in the creation of new states and the reorganization of boundaries to ensure that people speaking the same language were grouped together into one state.
 
• The Act led to the abolition of the distinction between Part A, Part B, Part C, and Part D states in India, streamlining the structure into a single category of states and union territories.

• Helped in administrative efficiency and governance by grouping people with common linguistic and cultural identities.

• **Anti-national activities** were defined under this Article as any activity or association that questioned, threatened, or undermined the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
• However, **Article 31D** was later repealed by the **44th Amendment Act, 1978**, which sought to restore the democratic balance in the Constitution post-Emergency.
 
• The 42nd Amendment Act is often referred to as the **“Mini-Constitution”** due to the extensive changes it brought to the Indian Constitution.
